# Tinyleaf

> Tinyleaf - Lightweight, zero-dependency web-based LaTeX editor

# Home

# Tinyleaf

**Lightweight, zero-dependency web-based LaTeX editor.**

Tinyleaf is a CLI-first LaTeX editor that runs in your browser. It requires no Python dependencies beyond the standard library, and supports both local and Docker-based compilation.

## Highlights

- **Zero dependencies** -- stdlib only (`http.server` + `threading` + `subprocess`)
- **Two modes** -- single project or multi-project with a persistent registry
- **Two compilation backends** -- local `latexmk` or Docker containers
- **CodeMirror 6** editor with LaTeX syntax highlighting
- **PDF.js** preview with live reload
- **Git integration** -- commit and push from the UI
- **7 themes** with dark/light toggle
- **i18n** -- English and Chinese

## Quick Start

```bash
pip install tinyleaf

# Single project
tinyleaf /path/to/my-thesis

# Multi-project (registry mode)
tinyleaf
```

## Links

- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/Oaklight/tinyleaf)
- [PyPI Package](https://pypi.org/project/tinyleaf/)

# Getting Started

# Installation

## From PyPI

```bash
pip install tinyleaf
```

## From Source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Oaklight/tinyleaf.git
cd tinyleaf
pip install -e .
```

## Requirements

- Python 3.8+
- No additional Python dependencies (stdlib only)

### Optional

- **Docker** -- for Docker-based compilation (`--docker` flag)
- **latexmk** -- for local compilation (default backend)
- A TeX Live distribution if compiling locally

# Quick Start

## Single Project Mode

Open a LaTeX project directory directly:

```bash
tinyleaf /path/to/my-thesis
```

This starts the editor on `http://localhost:14159` and opens it in your browser.

### With Docker Compilation

```bash
tinyleaf /path/to/my-thesis --docker
```

### Custom Port and Host

```bash
tinyleaf /path/to/my-thesis --port 3000 --host 0.0.0.0
```

## Multi-Project Mode

Launch without arguments to enter registry mode:

```bash
tinyleaf
```

From the project page you can:

- **Open Folder** -- browse the filesystem and register an existing directory
- **New Project** -- create a new LaTeX project at a chosen path
- **Remove** -- unregister a project (optionally delete files from disk)

Projects are stored in `~/.config/tinyleaf/projects.json`.

## Keyboard Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `Ctrl+S` | Save current file |
| `Ctrl+Enter` | Compile |
| `Ctrl+Shift+C` | Git commit |
| `Ctrl+Shift+P` | Git push |

# Guide

# Architecture

Tinyleaf is a single-binary web application built entirely with Python's standard library.

## Module Overview

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|---------------|
| `cli.py` | CLI argument parsing, server startup |
| `server.py` | HTTP routing, static file serving, SSE support |
| `handlers.py` | API request dispatch, file operations, project management |
| `registry.py` | Thread-safe project registry CRUD (`projects.json`) |
| `compiler.py` | LaTeX compilation jobs (local or Docker) |
| `git_ops.py` | Git status, diff, commit, push, pull, log |

## Key Design Decisions

- **Zero dependencies** -- only Python stdlib on the backend
- **Single HTML file** -- the entire frontend (HTML + CSS + JS) is served from one `index.html`
- **SSE for compilation** -- real-time log streaming via Server-Sent Events
- **Registry pattern** -- projects are tracked by name-to-path mapping in a JSON file, not by directory listing
- **Thread safety** -- `threading.Lock` + atomic `os.replace` for concurrent registry access

# Multi-Project Registry

When tinyleaf is launched without a `project_path` argument, it enters **multi-project mode** backed by a project registry.

## How It Works

Projects are stored in `~/.config/tinyleaf/projects.json`:

```json
{
  "my-thesis": {
    "path": "/home/user/documents/thesis",
    "added_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00"
  },
  "paper-2025": {
    "path": "/home/user/research/paper",
    "added_at": "2025-02-20T14:00:00"
  }
}
```

Each entry maps a project name to an **absolute filesystem path**. Projects can live anywhere -- they don't need to be in the same parent directory.

## Managing Projects

### From the UI

- **Open Folder** -- browse the server filesystem and register an existing directory
- **New Project** -- specify a name and parent path to create a new project with a default `main.tex`
- **Remove** -- unregister a project, with an optional checkbox to also delete files from disk

### CLI Options

```bash
# Registry mode (default when no path given)
tinyleaf

# Custom config directory
tinyleaf --config-dir /path/to/config

# Legacy migration: auto-register all subdirectories
tinyleaf --projects-dir /path/to/old/projects
```

## Stale Projects

If a registered project's directory no longer exists on disk, it is displayed with a dashed border and "(missing)" label. You can remove stale entries from the project page.

## Thread Safety

The registry uses a `threading.Lock` and atomic writes (`os.replace`) to ensure consistency under concurrent access from the threaded HTTP server.

# Compilation

Tinyleaf supports two compilation backends: **local** and **Docker**.

## Local Compilation (Default)

Uses `latexmk` installed on the host system:

```bash
tinyleaf /path/to/project
```

A TeX Live distribution with `latexmk` must be installed locally.

## Docker Compilation

Uses a Docker container with a full TeX Live installation:

```bash
tinyleaf /path/to/project --docker
```

The default Docker image is `oaklight/texlive:latest`. You can specify a different image:

```bash
tinyleaf /path/to/project --docker --image oaklight/texlive:science-cn
```

## Per-Project Configuration

Each project can have a `.tinyleaf.json` file to configure:

```json
{
  "main_file": "thesis.tex",
  "engine": "lualatex",
  "docker_image": "oaklight/texlive:science-cn"
}
```

| Field | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `main_file` | Auto-detected | The `.tex` file containing `\documentclass` |
| `engine` | `pdflatex` | LaTeX engine: `pdflatex`, `lualatex`, `xelatex` |
| `docker_image` | Server default | Override Docker image for this project |

## Auto-Detection

If `main_file` is not configured, tinyleaf scans for `.tex` files containing `\documentclass`. If exactly one is found, it is used. If multiple candidates exist, `main.tex` is preferred.

## Compilation Log

Compilation output is streamed in real-time via SSE (Server-Sent Events) to the browser log panel. Toggle the log panel with the log button in the toolbar.

# Docker

Tinyleaf can be deployed as a Docker container or use Docker for LaTeX compilation.

## Docker Compose Deployment

Run the editor itself inside a container:

```bash
docker compose up
```

This starts the web editor on `http://localhost:14159` with a persistent TeX Live container for compilation.

## Docker for Compilation Only

Use Docker only for the compilation step while running tinyleaf locally:

```bash
tinyleaf /path/to/project --docker --image oaklight/texlive:science-cn
```

### Available Images

The oaklight/texlive images provide various TeX Live configurations:

| Image | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `oaklight/texlive:latest` | Standard TeX Live |
| `oaklight/texlive:science` | Science packages |
| `oaklight/texlive:science-cn` | Science + Chinese fonts |
| `oaklight/texlive:science-jp` | Science + Japanese fonts |
| `oaklight/texlive:science-kr` | Science + Korean fonts |

### Font Cache

For faster subsequent compilations, Docker volume caching is recommended for font directories:

- `/root/.texlive2023/texmf-var`
- `/var/lib/texmf/luatex-cache`

# API Reference

Tinyleaf exposes a RESTful HTTP API consumed by the browser frontend.

## Endpoints

### Mode

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/api/mode` | Server mode and Docker config |
| `GET` | `/api/docker/images` | List local Docker images |

### Projects

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/api/projects` | List all registered projects |
| `POST` | `/api/projects` | Create a new project |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/register` | Register an existing directory |
| `DELETE` | `/api/projects/{name}` | Unregister (and optionally delete) a project |

### Filesystem Browser

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/api/fs/browse?path=...` | List subdirectories for the folder picker |

### Files

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/api/projects/{name}/files` | List file tree |
| `GET` | `/api/projects/{name}/files/{path}` | Read file content |
| `PUT` | `/api/projects/{name}/files/{path}` | Write file content |
| `DELETE` | `/api/projects/{name}/files/{path}` | Delete file or directory |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/{name}/mkdir` | Create a directory |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/{name}/rename` | Rename a file or directory |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/{name}/upload` | Upload files (multipart) |

### Configuration

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/api/projects/{name}/config` | Read project config |
| `PUT` | `/api/projects/{name}/config` | Update project config |

### Compilation

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `POST` | `/api/projects/{name}/compile` | Start compilation |
| `GET` | `/api/projects/{name}/compile/{id}/stream` | SSE compilation log stream |
| `GET` | `/api/projects/{name}/output/{file}` | Download compiled output |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/{name}/clean` | Remove build artifacts |

### Git

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/api/projects/{name}/git/status` | Git status |
| `GET` | `/api/projects/{name}/git/diff` | Git diff |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/{name}/git/commit` | Git commit |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/{name}/git/push` | Git push |
| `POST` | `/api/projects/{name}/git/pull` | Git pull |
| `GET` | `/api/projects/{name}/git/log` | Git log |

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [0.1.0] - 2026-04-27

Initial release of tinyleaf (formerly texlive-web).

### Added

- **CLI-first design** with `pip install tinyleaf && tinyleaf /path` to start editing
- **Single project mode** for opening a specific LaTeX project directory
- **Multi-project mode** with JSON-based project registry (`~/.config/tinyleaf/projects.json`)
- **Two compilation backends**: local `latexmk` (default) and Docker
- **CodeMirror 6** editor with LaTeX syntax highlighting
- **PDF.js** preview with live reload after compilation
- **SSE** (Server-Sent Events) real-time compilation log streaming
- **Git integration**: status, commit, push, and pull from the UI
- **i18n support** for English and Chinese
- **7 themes** with dark/light toggle (Light, Indigo Dark, Dracula, etc.)
- **Docker image selector** from locally available tags
- **Clean build artifacts** button
- **Auto-save** and window-focus file refresh
- **Keyboard shortcuts**: `Ctrl+S` (save), `Ctrl+Enter` (compile), `Ctrl+Shift+C` (commit), `Ctrl+Shift+P` (push)
- **Docker Compose** support for self-contained setup with Docker compilation
- **Zero Python dependencies** -- stdlib only (`http.server`, `threading`, `subprocess`)

### Changed

- Renamed project from `texlive-web` to `tinyleaf`
- Renamed Python package from `texlive_web` to `tinyleaf`
- Updated CLI entry point, config directory, and program name
- Updated project config file from `.texlive-web.json` to `.tinyleaf.json`
- Updated Docker image name to `oaklight/tinyleaf`
